title: Criterion verification runs without a human ADMIN command, so criterion receipts exist in an unattended run
description:
PREREQUISITE OF task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada, filed by architect-f04f69cf on 2026-09-09 because that row's DoD item 5 required this exact measurement before its plan could be submitted: "The planning architect records in planningNotes the measurement of whether criterion-runner is actually triggered in the normal journey at HEAD; if it is not, a prerequisite producer row is filed and named in dependsOn before this row's plan is submitted." It is not. This is that row.

WHAT I MEASURED AT HEAD, symbol by symbol, and it corrects a stale doc line in the parent's filing.

The parent's description notes that docs/plans/2026-09-06-repository-delivery-remediation.md:47 says "no composed producer yet" and calls that 3 days stale. It IS stale: the producer is composed. `daemon-repository-workflow-wiring.ts:15` builds `createCriterionEvidenceService`, `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:276` passes it through, and `daemon-command-registry.ts:417` dispatches `runCriterionCommandEdge` to it. `criterion-service.ts:24` constructs the runner. So composition is real and that half of the doc line should be corrected.

BUT COMPOSED IS NOT TRIGGERED, and the trigger is the gap:
- `criterion-runner.ts` is referenced by exactly ONE non-test module, `criterion-service.ts`, which is reached only through the command edge. There is no scheduler, no wrapper staffing, no coordinator call.
- The only producer of the verify offer is `criterion-read.ts:73-74`: `verifyOffer: artifact === null || pending || approvals.length !== goal.criteria.length ? null : offer(CRITERION_VERIFY, ...)`. So the offer does not even appear until an artifact exists, no run is pending, AND EVERY criterion is already approved.
- `verifyOffer` is consumed ONLY by the browser. A full-tree grep returns `apps/control-room/src/live/live-criterion-evidence.ts` and its tests, and nothing in the daemon.
- `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:179` maps BOTH kinds to ADMIN: `CRITERION_FAMILY = { [CRITERION_APPROVE]: CAPABILITIES.ADMIN, [CRITERION_VERIFY]: CAPABILITIES.ADMIN }`, and the registry reaches the criterion branch only after an OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED check at :410-414.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this blocks the parent rather than merely annoying it. The parent wants release evidence bound to criterion receipts, which is the right fix. But today a criterion receipt exists only after TWO human ADMIN commands per goal: approve every criterion, then verify. Bind release to that evidence with no automatic producer and an unattended release becomes IMPOSSIBLE rather than better-evidenced - the exact "narrowed DoD or mock-backed journey" outcome the rails forbid. The parent must land AFTER this row.

THE OWNER DIRECTION SHAPES THE ANSWER, 2026-09-09: "we can approve the plan at the start but that's it". Criterion APPROVAL is plausibly part of that one up-front approval and may legitimately stay human. VERIFICATION is a machine act - run the approved checks at the integrated sha and record what happened - and it is the half that must stop waiting for a person. Whoever plans this decides where the automatic trigger belongs and says why; do not assume the answer is a scheduler.

DO NOT WIDEN THE AUTHORIZATION FENCE to solve this. Making `criterion_check.verify` non-ADMIN, or handing an agent seat ADMIN, is a security change and is out of scope; the epic's rail is explicit that human gates stay human-only. The trigger must be an internal daemon act on its own principal, not a relaxation of who may command it from outside.
definitionOfDone: An arm proves a criterion run reaches COMPLETED with PASSED receipts for an approved goal WITHOUT any ADMIN-principal command being dispatched, asserting the run status and at least one receipt result, never merely that a run row appeared.

The authorization fence is unchanged and an arm proves it: `criterion_check.verify` and `criterion_check.approve` still map to ADMIN in CRITERION_FAMILY, and an external non-ADMIN caller is still refused with its stable code and layer.

The trigger's preconditions are asserted explicitly: no run is started when the integrated artifact is absent, when a run is already pending, or when any criterion lacks an approval — each asserted separately so the trigger cannot be a blanket.
Re-running the trigger for an already-COMPLETED run at the same integrated artifact does not start a second run, asserted by run count and by the reason the second attempt declined.

docs/plans/2026-09-06-repository-delivery-remediation.md:47's "no composed producer yet" line is corrected to the measured state: the producer IS composed (daemon-repository-workflow-wiring.ts:15, registry :417) and what this row adds is the trigger.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THE CORRECTION FIRST, THEN THE CHAIN. NO EDITS.

START WITH comment-b1022979 ON THIS ROW. I wrote this row's description and one load-bearing sentence in it is FALSE: "There is no scheduler, no wrapper staffing, no coordinator call." The runner IS driven on every wrapper pass. The row is still real and still blocks its parent, but it is SMALLER than filed. Plan against the comment, not against the description.

CONFIRM WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, because it is most of the machine:
- repository-delivery-runtime.ts:127-128 builds `createCriterionEvidenceService`; its `advance` at :136-142 runs `coordinator.advance()`, then `criteria.advance()`, then the publisher.
- agent-wrapper-main.ts:316 and :350 call `delivery.advance()` on the wrapper loop.
- criterion-runner.ts owns the entire execution path already: acquire a reservation (:149-151), transition to CRITERION_VERIFYING (:75), run each approved check, record receipts (:104-108), mark COMPLETED (:118), release with CRITERIA_COMPLETED (:63-64, :119) — all under `CRITERION_PRINCIPAL` (:54, :91).

CONFIRM THE ONE MISSING PIECE: `advance()` acts only on an already-QUEUED run (:146 blocks a non-QUEUED run it owns, :148 skips otherwise), and the sole producer of a QUEUED run is `queueCriterionVerification` (criterion-run.ts:43) behind the ADMIN command edge.

READ THE TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT KILL THE OBVIOUS APPROACH, and do not start writing until both are understood:
1. criterion-run.ts:52 — `if (!isDurableHumanPrincipal(store, input.principalId)) return criterionRefused("CRITERION_CHECK_HUMAN_REQUIRED");`. The daemon cannot call the existing function without fabricating a human principal.
2. criterion-run.ts:35-36 in `readCriterionRuns` — the first record for a runRef must be `status === "QUEUED"` AND `decisionTrace?.commandKind === CRITERION_VERIFY`, and any violation returns NULL FOR THE WHOLE CATALOGUE. A run written under a new kind without widening this makes evidence vanish for every reader, including goal closure and the parent row's dossier.

FINALLY, READ THE PRECONDITIONS YOU WILL REUSE: criterion-read.ts:73-74's `verifyOffer` gate — an integrated artifact exists, no run is pending, every criterion is approved — and note `queueCriterionVerification` re-checks the same three facts at :60 and :62-70. Those are the product's own answer to "is verification due?", and reusing them is what keeps the automatic and human paths from drifting.

implementationPlan.description:
ADD THE INTERNAL QUEUE PRODUCER, AND WIDEN THE READER IN THE SAME CHANGE (criterion-run.ts).

Write a second queue path beside `queueCriterionVerification`, not a modification of it. The human command keeps every check it has today, including `isDurableHumanPrincipal`. The internal path:
- runs on `CRITERION_PRINCIPAL`, the principal the runner already writes its own records under (criterion-runner.ts:54, :91), under its own internal command kind in the style of `internal.criterion.run` and `internal.criterion.started`;
- re-checks the SAME three preconditions server-side rather than trusting a caller: an integrated artifact exists and matches, no run is QUEUED / RUNNING / BLOCKED (the guard at :60), and every criterion carries an approval (:62-68);
- writes the identical `CriterionRun` shape with `status: "QUEUED"`, so the runner needs no change to consume it.

WIDEN `readCriterionRuns` AT :35-36 IN THE SAME EDIT. Today it demands `decisionTrace?.commandKind === CRITERION_VERIFY` on the first record and returns NULL for the entire catalogue otherwise. Accept the internal kind there too. Do this in the same commit as the producer: a producer without the reader widening does not fail loudly, it makes every consumer read an unreadable catalogue, which is evidence disappearing rather than an error.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE HUMAN PATH. `isDurableHumanPrincipal` stays on `queueCriterionVerification`, `CRITERION_FAMILY` keeps both kinds at ADMIN, and the registry's OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED check is untouched. This row adds a second, internal producer; it does not relax the first.

implementationPlan.description:
DRIVE THE PRODUCER FROM THE PASS THAT ALREADY RUNS (criterion-runner.ts, criterion-service.ts).

Call the internal queue from the existing `advance()` walk in criterion-runner.ts:123-156, before the QUEUED check. That walk already iterates `activeCompiledGraphs` for EXECUTION_ENABLED / CLOSING / COMPLETED, reads the goal and the latest run, and skips when `run === undefined` (:128) or when the run is not QUEUED (:148). Those are exactly the points where verification is due and nothing queues it.

DO NOT ADD A SECOND DRIVER. `advance()` is already called every wrapper pass at repository-delivery-runtime.ts:140. A timer or scheduler would race the existing pass for the same repository reservation.

RESPECT THE SERIALISATION AT :157-160 — `advancing ??= advance().finally(...)` makes concurrent calls share one in-flight pass. Queue INSIDE that pass so the guard covers the new work too; do not introduce an await that can deadlock against it.

DO NOT ADD A SECOND `acquire` PATH. The runner already acquires the compiled workspace at :149-151 and releases with CRITERIA_COMPLETED. Queuing only writes a run record; the existing acquire then picks it up on the same or the next pass. A separate reservation would contend with the delivery coordinator for the same checkout — and an unreleased reservation is precisely what wedges a checkout in the sibling row task-9dbe28fdccc546dfbbbf9b32f68e7c61.

criterion-service.ts needs no new public surface unless the queue helper has to be injected for tests; if it does, follow the existing `executor` and `repository` test-seam pattern at :19-20 rather than inventing a third convention.
implementationPlan.note: Hooked real internal queue inside existing serialized advance pass, only when repository.readOwned proves no held reservation. Existing completed-run release/recovery takes precedence, avoiding replacing its runRef with a newly queued artifact while old ownership remains. implementationPlan.description:
THE ARMS (DoD 1, 2, 3, 4), each asserting a reason rather than an outcome.

(a) THE ROW'S POINT, in criterion-runner-recovery.test.ts or criterion-run.test.ts as fits the fixture — a criterion run reaches COMPLETED with PASSED receipts for an approved goal with NO ADMIN-principal command dispatched. Assert the run STATUS and at least one receipt RESULT, never merely that a run row appeared (DoD 1). The executor and repository test seams may be used to keep it fast, but the QUEUE step must be the real internal producer, since that is the thing this row adds.

(b) THE FENCE IS UNCHANGED (DoD 2) — `CRITERION_FAMILY` still maps both `criterion_check.verify` and `criterion_check.approve` to ADMIN, and an external non-ADMIN caller is still refused with its stable code and layer. Also assert `queueCriterionVerification` still refuses CRITERION_CHECK_HUMAN_REQUIRED for a non-human principal: the internal path must not have been built by weakening the human one.

(c) THE PRECONDITIONS, EACH SEPARATELY (DoD 3) — no run is queued when the integrated artifact is absent, when a run is already pending, and when any criterion lacks an approval. Three arms, not one compound arm: a single "nothing happened" assertion cannot tell which guard fired, and a trigger that fires on the wrong one is a blanket.

(d) IDEMPOTENCE (DoD 4) — running the trigger again for an already-COMPLETED run at the same integrated artifact does not start a second run. Assert the run COUNT and the reason the second attempt declined.

(e) THE READER SURVIVES (the constraint from step 2) — `readCriterionRuns` returns a readable catalogue for an internally-queued run, and `readCriterionEvidence` still reports its criteria. Without this arm the widening at criterion-run.ts:35-36 is untested and a later tightening would make evidence vanish silently.
implementationPlan.note: Added explicit ADMIN roster plus HTTP non-ADMIN CAPABILITY_DENIED@AUTHORIZE arms for both kinds, preserved CRITERION_CHECK_HUMAN_REQUIRED@CRITERION_EVIDENCE for human queue. comments.author: architect-f04f69cf
comments.content:
CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION, BY ITS AUTHOR. architect-f04f69cf, 2026-09-09, planning it. The row is still real and still blocks its parent, but one load-bearing sentence in the description is FALSE and the gap is narrower and better-shaped than I filed it.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. The description says "There is no scheduler, no wrapper staffing, no coordinator call." That is false. The runner IS driven on every wrapper pass:
- repository-delivery-runtime.ts:127-128 builds `createCriterionEvidenceService`, and its `advance` at :136-142 calls `coordinator.advance()`, then `criteria.advance()`, then the publisher.
- agent-wrapper-main.ts:316 and :350 call `delivery.advance()` on the wrapper loop.
I reached the wrong conclusion by grepping for importers of `criterion-runner.ts` and stopping there; I never grepped `.advance()` call sites until I planned the row. The importer graph answers "what is composed", not "what is called".

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING, measured precisely. `advance()` only acts on a run that is already QUEUED — criterion-runner.ts:146 blocks any non-QUEUED run it owns and :148 skips when `run.status !== "QUEUED"`. The ONLY producer of a QUEUED run is `queueCriterionVerification` (criterion-run.ts:43), reached solely through `criterion-service.ts:34 verify()` behind the ADMIN command edge. So the executor is wired and idling; nothing ever puts work in front of it without a human.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT SHAPE THE FIX, and both would stop a worker cold at implementation time if the plan did not name them:
1. `queueCriterionVerification` at criterion-run.ts:52 requires `isDurableHumanPrincipal(store, input.principalId)` and otherwise refuses CRITERION_CHECK_HUMAN_REQUIRED. A human principal is demanded by an explicit check, not merely by the ADMIN capability map — so "just call the existing function from the daemon" does not work and must not be forced by faking a principal.
2. `readCriterionRuns` at criterion-run.ts:35-36 requires the FIRST record of each runRef to be `status === "QUEUED"` AND `row.event.decisionTrace?.commandKind === CRITERION_VERIFY`, and returns NULL for the whole read otherwise. A run queued under any other command kind makes every reader see an unreadable catalogue — including `readCriterionEvidence`, the release dossier work in the parent row, and goal closure. So the reader must accept the internal kind in the same change, or nothing can read what the trigger writes.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SCOPE. The row is SMALLER than filed: no scheduler and no new execution path, because both already exist. It is one internal queue producer plus the reader widening, gated on exactly the conditions `criterion-read.ts:73-74` already uses to decide whether to offer a human the verify button — an integrated artifact exists, no run is pending, and every criterion is approved.

UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDING: DoD 2's fence clause. `CRITERION_FAMILY` keeps both kinds at ADMIN, an external non-ADMIN caller is still refused, and the internal trigger runs on `CRITERION_PRINCIPAL` — the principal the runner already writes its own records under (criterion-runner.ts:53-54, :91). The fix is a second, internal producer beside the human one, never a relaxation of the human one.

DoD 5's doc correction also needs widening: docs/plans/2026-09-06-repository-delivery-remediation.md:47 says criterion evidence "has no composed producer yet", and the truth is that it is composed AND driven, and what is missing is only the queue.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (step-5), answering the five questions the step asked, in order. No fix-now defect found; two deliberate behaviours disclosed rather than changed.

1. HUMAN AND AUTOMATIC ON THE SAME PASS - WHICH WINS, CAN BOTH WRITE? Neither can double-write. The internal producer snapshots `getAggregateVersion` on the runs aggregate BEFORE reading the catalogues and the artifact, then commits at that `expectedVersion`. Anything landing in between makes the commit lose the compare-and-swap. Proven by the two `loses the run CAS to a competing %s queue` arms (human verify, and a second automatic queue), each asserting `CRITERION_CHECK_VERSION_CONFLICT` and the aggregate at version 1. The stale-version window is fail-closed in the safe direction: a stale-LOW expectedVersion can only refuse, never overwrite. Within one process the `advancing ??=` guard at criterion-runner.ts:157-160 already serialises, and the `Promise.all` arm shows 3 events for two concurrent passes.

2. ARTIFACT CHANGES BETWEEN QUEUE AND EXECUTE - INHERITED OR BYPASSED? Inherited, because the internal path writes the identical `CriterionRun` shape and is executed by the same unmodified code, so criterion-runner.ts:74, :98 and :116 re-check `sameCriterionArtifact` exactly as they do for a human-queued run. Arm `retains artifact fences when it changes before/during automatic execution` proves both timings: changed BEFORE execution the executor is never called; changed DURING (mutated inside the check) it is called once, and in both cases the run ends BLOCKED, the reservation is BLOCKED, and the reservation is NOT released. Verified from the fence, not from the design.

3. DOES IT KEEP FIRING ON A BLOCKED RUN - RETRY LOOP? No. The guard is `runs.some((run) => run.status !== "COMPLETED")` -> `CRITERION_CHECK_RUN_PENDING`, which covers BLOCKED as well as QUEUED and RUNNING, asserted in the parameterised idempotence arm. DISCLOSED CONSEQUENCE, deliberate: a BLOCKED batch is never automatically retried, and neither is a COMPLETED batch whose receipts FAILED, since the artifact-equality decline is status-blind. Recovery is a human explicit verify, or a new integrated artifact. Chosen over auto-retry because a self-retrying failed check at an unchanged sha is an unbounded loop that also re-acquires the repository reservation each time. Commented in source at criterion-run.ts.

4. CAN A CLOSING / COMPLETED GOAL BE QUEUED AFTER CLOSURE? Yes, and this is a real behaviour change worth QA's eye rather than a bug I am hiding. `activeCompiledGraphs` at criterion-runner.ts:125 filters EXECUTION_ENABLED, CLOSING and COMPLETED, and I did not narrow it - narrowing it would have changed which goals the EXISTING runner advances, which is outside this row. Effect: a closed goal that gains a new integrated artifact, with every criterion still approved and no pending run, gets one fresh run at that artifact. It is bounded - one run per distinct artifact, then ALREADY_COMPLETED - so it is not a loop, and re-verifying a closed goal at a new sha is evidence a reader wants. Flagging it because the alternative reading (evidence should freeze at closure) is defensible and is a one-line filter change if the epic wants it.

5. DOES AN UNATTENDED RUN NOW PRODUCE RECEIPTS, AND WHICH ARM PROVES IT? Yes. The arm is criterion-runner-recovery.test.ts `automatically completes approved checks without a human verification command`. It points at behaviour, not design: it drives the real `queueAutomaticCriterionVerification` through the real `service.advance()` (only the executor and repository test seams are substituted, as the plan permits), and asserts COMPLETED with `status: "PASSED"` on both criteria, `service.verify` never called, and every run event's decisionTrace principal equal to CRITERION_PRINCIPAL. No ADMIN-principal command is dispatched anywhere in that arm.

CHECKLIST ITEMS WITH NOTHING TO REPORT: no handle, socket or subprocess is opened by the queue - it writes one record and takes no reservation, and it only runs when `owned.handle === null`, so a completed batch's release path always precedes queuing a different artifact (own arm). Malformed and throwing artifact readers are contained to `CRITERION_CHECK_UNREADABLE` with the aggregate untouched. A zero-criteria goal is excluded explicitly by `approved.length === 0`, which the `!==` length comparison alone would have let through.
